title: Point-in-time recovery: the target, the timeline and the rehearsal

videos.script: Orders arrive, one a second. In the middle of them, somebody runs a DELETE against the wrong database. {{mistake}} Twelve thousand orders are gone, and the orders before and after it are real sales. {{both}} A dump would bring back the old orders and lose the new ones. In this lesson you go back to the exact moment before the mistake. {{moment}} First you find it, in the log itself. One transaction deleted twelve thousand rows, and the log says when it committed. {{waldump}} The first restore fails, because the moment you want is not in the archive yet. {{fail}} The second one stops right before the mistake, and waits for you to look. {{pause}} Then you choose: replace the live database, or repair it from the copy. {{repair}} And you meet timelines, the way PostgreSQL keeps two histories apart.
